# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jan 30, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing protocol security with new AI and Semgrep rules, improving deployment script robustness, and refining the Superchain ecosystem's testing infrastructure. Several bug fixes addressed critical issues in upgrade processes and websocket handling, alongside significant updates to Kona prestate builds.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Enhanced Protocol Security and Code Safety
New features were introduced to bolster protocol security. Graphite rules were updated to review storage layout changes for potential unsafe modifications ([#19004](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19004)). Additionally, a Semgrep rule was added to prevent `initialize` functions on the L1 side from lacking proper `assertOnlyProxyAdminOrProxyAdminOwner` checks ([#19002](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19002)).

### Improved Deployment and Upgrade Process Reliability
Several fixes targeted the reliability of deployment and upgrade scripts. Errors in OPCM upgrade calls now surface the real revert reason instead of generic messages in `UpgradeOPChain` and `UpgradeSuperchainConfig` ([#19005](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19005)). The `DelayedWETH` implementation is now sourced directly from `OPCM.implementations()`, removing the need to fetch the proxy ([#19003](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19003)). A code length check was also added for `ReadSuperchainDeployment` in OPCM v2 to ensure correct `superchainConfigProxy` validation ([#19021](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19021)).

### Superchain Ecosystem and Testing Infrastructure Updates
Significant work was done to support the Superchain ecosystem and testing. The `op-acceptance-test` now supports creating honest trace accessors for super games, enhancing dispute game testing capabilities ([#18978](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18978)). A test was added to confirm that OPCMv2 can perform upgrades even when paused ([#19019](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19019)). Kona prestate builds were updated to use local sources and remove asterisk support, improving reproducibility ([#18879](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18879)). The Supernode is now exposed in the `sysgo` system within `op-devstack` to be visible to components like `op-challenger` ([#18986](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18986)).

### General Bug Fixes and Maintenance
A fix addressed an unbound variable error in `build-prestates.sh` ([#19026](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19026)). The websocket read limit in `op-service` was increased to 10MB to prevent failures when reading the Flashblocks websocket stream ([#19024](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19024)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS

- [#19036](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19036) feat: add starting AGENTS.md file
- [#19035](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19035) feat: no beta tags in production upgrade

- [#19032](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19032) txmgr: move BlobTipOracle ownership to txmgr
- [#19031](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19031) Add workaround for old buildx version
- [#19030](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19030) feat(flashblocks): add transaction caching to avoid re-executing unchanged transactions (4)
- [#19029](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19029) devstack: Integrate supernode features for proof tests

- [#19020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19020) ci: test factory reusable workflow upgrade

## CLOSED ISSUES
### Kona Prestate Validation Simplified
The issue concerning the simplification of Kona prestate validation ([#18735](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18735)) has been closed. This likely reflects the successful integration of Kona into the monorepo and the streamlining of its build processes.

## NEW ISSUES
### op-rbuilder RPC Server for Throttling
A new issue has been opened regarding the `op-rbuilder` RPC server for throttling ([#19023](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19023)). The core problem is that while `op-rbuilder` implements block throttling, it doesn't expose the `miner_setMaxDASize` RPC endpoint, which the batcher needs to set throttling parameters.

## ACTIVE ISSUES
### op-node: Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17631))
Discussion continues on the behavior of `op-node`'s initial EL Sync. The main concern is that `op-node` marks the reached target as finalized even if the block isn't truly finalized, which was an intended design choice. The latest comment from `trianglesphere` clarifies that this behavior, while now considered a bug, was part of the original design, and re-running derivation on a snap-synced node doesn't work as expected.

### chore(kona/proofs): remove outdated just recipes once kona's migration is complete ([#18654](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18654))
This issue, previously closed, has been reopened by `ajsutton` due to a remaining TODO in the code related to outdated `just` recipes. The goal is to remove custom `just` recipes for building `kona-host/client` now that Kona's migration into the monorepo is complete.

### op-reth: batcher throttling ([#18764](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18764))
The discussion revolves around implementing batcher throttling in `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder`. `einar-oplabs` clarified that the throttling mechanism should be exposed via JSON-RPC, not just CLI parameters, to align with existing batcher communication. `sebastianst` emphasized that both programs should support the existing RPCs via HTTP. Progress has been made on `op-reth`'s throttle logic and JSON-RPC, with tests in progress. For `op-rbuilder`, throttle logic and tests are in place, but adding a JSON-RPC server and endpoint is still pending.

### op-supernode: Safe Label Adjusting ([#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18976))
The conversation focuses on how the `op-supernode` should manage and interpret "safe" labels across different layers (EL, CL, Super). `axelKingsley` praised the proposed diagram and terminology, highlighting the importance of distinguishing between "Local Safe" and "Super Node" verified states. The main concern is ensuring the CL doesn't get "upset" if its local safe payloads don't stick, and how the RPC router should handle these different safe labels. `geoknee` provided a detailed proposal, including options for adorning ELs with new labels like "local safe" or having the supernode communicate directly with the CL to infer block safety, to avoid deadlocks if the EL's safe label is controlled by the supernode. The current interop activity queries the EL for the safe block, which would lead to a deadlock if the EL's safe label is only updated after cross-safety is established by the supernode.
